messages:
maya: morning — Nora from AcmeApp opened a support ticket: rerank endpoint returns 500s intermittently when their CSV-derived inputs contain emojis and occasional null bytes. attaching logs from the request and the customer repro below. escalation to eng requested.

nora_acme: hey team — we've been seeing failures only on certain rows after a nightly ETL. quick snippet of the failing request (we redacted PII):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-...\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"query":"Which article is best?","candidates":["Best practices for emojis 👍","Null test:\u0000 end","Plain text"]}'
```
The 2nd candidate has a null byte in the middle (we suspect from a CSV escape) and sometimes emojis. Response is a 500 with a short error in the body: `{\"error\":\"internal server error\"}` and the support log shows: `invalid utf-8 sequence at byte 28` then a stacktrace in the model host.

maya: thanks Nora. can you paste the full raw body as bytes (hex) or upload the row to the ticket? also, does removing the null byte make the request succeed?

nora_acme: removing the \u0000 fixes it. examples here (we converted to hex):
- candidate 2 bytes: 42 65 73 74 20 74 65 73 74 3a 00 20 65 6e 64
- candidate 1 (with emoji) UTF-8 bytes: 42 65 73 74 20 70 72 61 63 74 69 63 65 73 20 f0 9f 91 8d
So emoji bytes seem fine. the null is the main trigger.

sam: assigning to eng-oncall (sam). initial hypothesis: NUL bytes are not allowed by our tokenizer/serving runtime and are blowing up a C/C++ library that expects valid UTF-8 without NULs. we should surface as 400 with a validation error instead of 500.

sam: repro steps I ran locally (on prod-like image):
```python
import requests
body = {
  \"query\": \"Which article?\",
  \"candidates\": [\"Good emoji 👍\", \"Bad\u0000Null\", \"Other\"]
}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', json=body, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer internal-debug'})
print(r.status_code)
print(r.text)
```
I can reproduce 500 and a backtrace in the model host log: `Assertion failed: !contains_nul(buffer)` then an abort.

eli: adding context from reranker pipeline — the reranker uses a tokenizer written in Rust/C++ that maps raw bytes and passes a null-terminated C string into downstream native ops. Null bytes terminate the string unexpectedly which produces corrupted token ids and occasionally OOB reads leading to crashes or garbage scores. Emojis are okay if encoded as valid UTF-8 sequences.

eli: quick mitigation options:
- immediate workaround for customers: strip NULs before sending (replace \u0000 with empty string) or base64-encode candidate strings and add a metadata header (ugh but workable).
- short-term server fix: validate input at gateway and return 400 with a helpful message (\"invalid character: NUL byte in candidate at index X\").
- medium-term: sanitize inputs in the runtime (replace NULs with U+FFFD or remove) and add unit tests to the tokenizer to reject inputs containing control characters.

maya: can we get a patch for the gateway 400 behavior? customers should get actionable errors.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to do validation+clear 400 at the API layer (reject if any candidate contains a NUL or non-decodable UTF-8). if runtime still crashes we patch runtime sanitizer. plan: validate in the API handler, log metrics (invalid_payload_utf8), and surface a UA-friendly message.

sam: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/593 - adds utf8 validation in the rerank handler and tests. marking as staged for canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime PR 593 to canary cluster (canary-2).

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded — runtime PR 593 rolled to canary-2 at revision 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z.

maya: rolled the change to the customer's account (they're on canary region) and asked them to retry. Nora confirmed: the exact same payload that previously 500s now returns 400 with body: `{\"error\":\"invalid request: candidate contains disallowed NUL byte at index 1\"}` — much better.

nora_acme: thanks, that error is actionable. we'll strip NULs in our ETL too. curious if you can also document best practices for CSV imports causing stray NULs?

eli: will add a short KB note: recommend normalizing to NFC, strip control characters (0x00..0x1F except valid whitespace), validate UTF-8, and optionally escape binary via base64 if the field may contain binary. I'll add it to the devdocs and link in the support KB.

maya: closing loop — customer patched ETL, no further incidents reported. followups: create KB article and add a metric dashboard for invalid_payload_utf8.

sam: follow-up ticket filed for runtime hardening (sanitize on host) and adding fuzz tests for tokenizer. ticket: INTG-1287.

maya: thanks all — nice quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
